lead.text: Reverion has raised a huge €154.2m to mass-produce the most efficient thermal power plant anyone has measured. The idea started in 2015 in Stephan Herrmann's doctorate at TU Munich and became a company in 2022, in Eresing in rural Bavaria. It builds solid oxide fuel cell plants that turn natural gas, biogas or hydrogen straight into electricity at 74.2% electrical efficiency, run backwards to store energy, and can be carbon negative when fed biogas. Kembara, the €1bn deeptech and climate fund at Mundi Ventures, led, with Allianz, KfW Capital, Aurum Impact and Carbon Equity new alongside Extantia, Energy Impact Partners, UVC Partners and the EIC Fund. The money goes into a second German factory, 250 megawatts a year and up to 800 jobs. Clean power on tap, as the founder puts it, rather than clean power when the weather allows.

source.title: Germany's Reverion raises €154.2 million to scale production of power plants that generate electricity from gas

lead.investorsLabel: Kembara, Allianz, KfW Capital, Aurum Impact, Carbon Equity, Extantia, Energy Impact Partners, UVC Partners, European Innovation Council Fund and Possible Ventures

lead.text: Kuro has raised €10m to take the paperwork off general contractors. Founded in November 2024 by Lea Scherer and Jonas Minkler, who came out of alcemy and Capmo, the Berlin company sits where every construction project is actually decided, in estimating, procurement, accounting and compliance, and is starting with estimating before working outwards. UVC Partners led, with Foundamental, Realyze Ventures and helloworld following on. Sixteen people, a growing list of large contractors, and two years old next month.

source.title: Berlin-based Kuro raises €10 million to build the AI foundation for general contractors

lead.investorsLabel: UVC Partners, Foundamental, Realyze Ventures and helloworld

lead.text: Noxtua has raised more than €100m, and in the same breath sold control. C.H.BECK, the legal publisher German lawyers have been reading for two centuries, becomes majority shareholder, with MANZ joining as a new investor and Global Brain, the KDDI Open Innovation Fund, CMS and Dentons on the way out. Noxtua builds sovereign legal AI, trained and hosted in Europe for firms that cannot send a client file to an American model. For a legaltech company, being bought into by the publisher whose commentaries are the ground truth is either the best distribution deal available or the end of being a startup, and possibly both.

note.text: C.H.BECK becomes the majority shareholder with this round, so Noxtua is no longer independently owned.

source.title: Noxtua raises more than €100M as C.H.BECK takes majority stake in legaltech

lead.text: Metycle has secured a €131.7m credit facility to buy more scrap metal. Founded in 2022 by Rafael Suchan and Sebastian Brenner, the Cologne company buys, upgrades and supplies recycled copper and aluminium to industrial customers, in a market that runs on trust, paper and long-standing relationships. The facility comes from Rivonia Road Capital, a Californian asset-backed lender, and it is working capital rather than equity, which is what a company that has to own metal before it can sell it actually needs. Its last equity round was €14m in February 2025.

source.title: Cologne-based Metycle secures €131.7 million credit facility to scale secondary copper and aluminium supply

lead.text: Integral has raised €18m to put AI agents and licensed accountants on the same team. Founded in Berlin by Lukas Zörner and Anil Can Baykal, Integral does the accounting, tax and payroll for small and mid-sized companies itself rather than selling them software to do it, with agents taking the repetitive half of the job, the invoice reconciliation and the filings, and qualified professionals signing off the rest. Mosaic Ventures and Reid Hoffman co-led, with Cherry Ventures, General Catalyst and Puzzle Ventures following on. That makes two German rounds in a month aimed squarely at the tax profession, after Limetax in September.

lead.text: Arcos has raised €5.5m to watch over the buildings nobody is watching. Founded by Louis Wübben and Moritz Steigerwald, the Munich company puts sensors and an incident system on one platform, so a single control room can cover housing, commercial sites and critical infrastructure instead of each running its own. High-Tech Gründerfonds led the seed round, with Bayern Kapital, Pact, Haufe and Robin Capital following on. Civil safety is quietly becoming a category in Germany, and this is the week's second round in it.

lead.text: The Exploration Company has raised a huge $450m Series C, which it calls the largest ever raised by a European space company. Founded by Hélène Huby and based in Munich and Bordeaux, TEC builds Nyx, a reusable capsule designed to dock with the International Space Station and come back to Earth, and it is now accelerating Storm, a high-thrust reusable rocket engine. Bessemer Venture Partners, Atomico and the Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT co-led, with Balderton, Plural, Cherry and Red River West following on. That takes total funding to about $680m. No valuation was disclosed, so it does not enter the register yet. Three days later it won ESA's ALADDIN cargo capsule contract, worth €760m.

source.title: The Exploration Company nabs $450 million to challenge SpaceX

lead.text: Limetax has raised €36m to bring German tax firms together and run them on AI. Founded in Berlin by Christoph Gamon, Maximilian Meyer and Christoph Dansard, who between them came through Razor Group, N26 and Augustus, Limetax brings established tax and accounting firms into one group and makes its own agentic platform the backbone of their daily work. Motive Partners led the €6m pre-seed equity with Activant and Heliad, alongside former finance minister Christian Lindner and the Moss founders Anton Rummel and Ante Spittler, and a consortium of German banks put up a €30m credit facility. Germany has nearly 54,000 of these firms and not enough qualified people to staff them. Limetax only launched in January.

note.text: €30m of the €36m is a credit facility from a consortium of German banks, and €6m is pre-seed equity.

lead.text: HyImpulse has raised more than €50m in equity to take its own rockets to orbit. Spun out of the German Aerospace Centre in 2018 by Christian Schmierer, Mario Kobald, Konstantin Tomilin and Ulrich Fischer, the company from Neuenstadt am Kocher builds hybrid rockets that burn paraffin with liquid oxygen, a non-explosive combination it says is safer and cheaper than kerosene, and it already operates a commercial suborbital platform. JOIN Capital and Ace Capital Partners co-led the Series A extension, with North Ventures, BW-Capital, Bayern Kapital and the German Aerospace Centre itself joining and Campus Founders Ventures following on. That takes its equity and public funding past €125m. A European launcher, built in a small town in Baden-Württemberg.

lead.text: INLEAP Photonics has raised around €20m to stop drones with light. Founded in Hanover by Marius Lammers, INLEAP builds ultra-fast, high-precision laser beam steering, the part of a counter-drone system that puts a laser on a small, fast target and keeps it there, for the military and for critical infrastructure. UVC Partners led the seed round, with High-Tech Gründerfonds, Poland's Balnord, Estonia's Sentris and Denmark's Scale Capital following on. Investors from four countries in a single seed round, for a capability Europe has decided it needs at home.

lead.text: Revier Therapeutics has launched with €6m to go after the biology behind heart disease. Founded in Heidelberg by Prof. Eva van Rooij and Prof. Johannes Backs, Revier is the first company to selectively target class IIa HDACs, enzymes that drive cardiometabolic disease, with small molecules taken by mouth that block the damaging activity and leave healthy function alone. First up are two conditions with few targeted treatments, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Round led by the KHAN Technology Transfer Fund II, with High-Tech Gründerfonds, VORNvc and private investors through Revier Invest Heidelberg following on. It came out of stealth and closed the round in the same announcement.

lead.text: Kazimi has raised €2.2m to tell mobile apps which of their users are real. Founded in Berlin in 2024 by August Joseph, Chase Gummer, Ville Mikkola and Andreas Naumann, Kazimi secures the signals an app sends home, so a developer can verify its first-party data and separate genuine users from bots, using cryptography and zero-knowledge proofs. The oversubscribed pre-seed was led by Market One Capital with IBB Ventures following on, alongside former Rovio CTO Petri Hyökyranta, former Supercell data scientist Janne Peltola and Erik Massmann, once CFO of the Birkenstock Group. Mobile gaming studios are already customers. Cloudflare reported this year that bot activity overtook human activity online for the first time, which is the whole market in one sentence.

lead.text: Flip has raised €22m to get AI onto the factory floor. Founded in Stuttgart in 2018, Flip builds the app for the eighty percent of employees who do not work at a desk, in production, retail, logistics, care and hospitality, and it now carries digital identity and AI agents alongside the shift plan. Notion Capital and HV Capital both doubled down, with L-Bank, the development bank of Baden-Württemberg, joining as a new investor. Bosch, REWE, SIXT and FORVIA HELLA are already running it. Benedikt Brand puts the gap plainly, that AI has long been part of everyday life in the office and has barely arrived on the assembly line.

lead.investorsLabel: Notion Capital, HV Capital and L-Bank

lead.text: Oceanloop has secured up to €38.5m to farm fish on land. Formed in 2023 out of the merger of Crusta Nova, one of Europe's first commercial shrimp producers, with the marine systems expertise of Sander, the Munich company builds recirculating aquaculture systems, which are closed tanks run on water treatment and software rather than open sea cages. It is the first company to farm Giant Grouper in Europe, and sales from the farm at Strande near Kiel started in April. Hatch Blue and Stolt Ventures put in the equity and the European Investment Bank the venture debt. Next comes a 250 ton farm in Kiel by the end of the year, then 2,000 tons on Gran Canaria.

note.text: €32m of the €38.5m is a European Investment Bank venture-debt facility rather than equity.

lead.text: NavVis has raised a huge €73.7m Series D. Spun out of the Technical University of Munich thirteen years ago by four researchers, NavVis maps the inside of factories, plants and the mission-critical infrastructure nobody photographs, and keeps the digital copy synchronised with the physical one. Round led by the American private equity firm The Jordan Company, with Yttrium, KOZO KEIKAKU ENGINEERING and Cipio Partners following on. Felix Reinshagen says customers trust it with billions of square metres of that data. Thirteen years of unfashionable engineering, a growth round from abroad, and the headquarters still in Munich.
